title: Build an Integration
snippet:
## Dev/test organization
If you need a separate Close organization for development and testing:
- **Already a Close user** — You can create a free secondary organization. See [Secondary organization](https://help.close.com/docs/secondary-organization) for instructions.
- **Not a Close user** — Integration partners who don’t use Close in their own sales process can request a free Dev organization by emailing [support@close.com](mailto:support@close.com) with a description of your OAuth app, the overall workflow, and your expected release timeline. Dev organizations work identically to standard Close organizations but have no subscription fees.
Your OAuth app continues to work regardless of whether your Close account’s subscription is active, expired, or canceled.

title: help.close.com/docs/ai-credits
snippet:
Close uses a credit-based system to power advanced AI features. Credits are pooled at the account level, reset monthly, and do not roll over.
Close has three separate billing areas: your **CRM plan**, **telephony usage** (calls, SMS, and phone numbers), and **AI credits**. These are billed and invoiced separately. This article covers AI credits only. See [Calling and SMS Usage](/account-management/variable-usage-costs-calling-sms-phone-numbers-ai-tools) for telephony rates.
Some AI features are **always free** — they never consume credits and keep working even if your balance hits zero.

Is Close free?
Close doesn’t have a free plan, but you can try it free for 14 days with no credit card. The trial includes calling and AI credits, so you can call real leads and try Chloe and AI Agents before you pay. After the trial, plans start at $9/month for Solo, billed annually.

Does Close include API access?
Yes. Close provides a REST API for building custom integrations, connecting your applications, and automating sales processes. API requests are subject to rate limits, but Close does not have a published daily API request quota or separate per-request API fees.
[Explore the Close API](https://developer.close.com/)
Does Close have API rate limits?
Yes. Close uses endpoint-specific rate limits to maintain reliability. Many commonly used endpoints support high request volumes, allowing businesses to build integrations, AI agents, and automations without a daily API request quota. Limits vary by endpoint.

title: Attio vs Close: which one, and why
snippet:
| Compare | [Attio API](/gtm-apis/crm-apis/attio-api-review) | [Close](https://www.close.com/) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | A CRM whose data model you define in code | API on every plan, and the org limit is three times the key limit |
| Entry price | $44/user/mo | $19/seat/mo |
| Unit cost | Not sold by the unit | Not sold by the unit |
| Billing model | Per seat Subscription Free tier | Per seat Subscription |
| Free tier | Free plan with full API access, 100 seat credits a month | No free tier. Free trial, and $9 a seat a month on Solo billed annually. |
| GTM motion covered | Sync | Sync Engage |
| Data returned | CRM recordsWork emailFirmographics | CRM recordsWork emailFirmographics |
| MCP server | Yes Part of the Attio developer platform | Yes https://developer.close.com/mcp |
| Interfaces | REST API MCP server Webhooks n8n node | REST API MCP server Webhooks Bulk or async |
| Auth | Bearer token or OAuth 2.0 | API key, or OAuth 2.0 for user-facing integrations |
| Rate limits | 100 requests/s for reads, 25/s for writes, across the whole API | Per endpoint group. Published as a structure rather than as numbers; read the RateLimit header. |
| Coverage | Global | Global |
| Compliance | GDPR DPA SOC 2 Type II | GDPR DPA CCPA |
| Best for | Best API-first CRM | Inside sales CRM with calling built in |
